summary: Frede Møller-Kristensen was an Indologist who earned an M.A. from the University of Copenhagen in 1960. He served as a lecturer in Pāli at the University of Copenhagen (1966-1972) and Director of the Oriental Department at the Royal Danish Library (1969-1987).

Frederic Salmon Growse was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at Oriel College and The Queen's College, Oxford (B.A. 1859). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1860-1891) and was a Fellow of the University of Calcutta.
Frederic Spring worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society and was a chaplain with the Madras Army until 1824.

Indologist Frederick Eden Pargiter studied at Taunton Grammar School and Exeter College. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1875-1906), as a judge on the Calcutta High Court (1904-1906), and as president of The Asiatic Society (1903-1905).

Frederick J. Streng worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, earning degrees from Texas Lutheran, SMU, and Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He taught at the University of Southern California (1963-1966) and Southern Methodist University (1966-1974).

Frederick James Furnivall was a linguist who studied at University College London and Trinity Hall. He founded multiple literary societies, taught at the Working Men's College (~1854-1910), and served as secretary of the Philological Society (1853-1910).

Frederick M. Asher was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities (~1970-2017), where he became a professor around 1980, and was attested at the Library of Congress in 1993.

Frederick M. Smith is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, George Cardona, Wilhelm Halbfass, and Agnihothram Ramanuja Tatachariar. He held professorships at the University of Iowa.

Frederick Price was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at the University of Melbourne (~1856-1859). He served in the Madras Civil Service from 1862 to 1897, holding the post of Chief Secretary to the Government of Madras.

Frederick William Thomas was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Chief Librarian at the India Office (1903-1927) and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927-1937).

Frederick Zeuner was an archaeologist who completed his Ph.D. at Breslau after studying at Berlin and Tübingen. He held posts at the University of London, including Professor of Environmental Archaeology (1946) and at the UCL Institute of Archaeology (~1934-1963).

Frederik David Kan Bosch studied Indology and archaeology at Leiden University under Jacob Speyer and Jean Philippe Vogel. He directed the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1916-1936) and held professorships at Utrecht (1938-1945) and Leiden (1946-1957).

Fredrik Barth studied anthropology at the University of Chicago and the University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He founded anthropology at the University of Bergen (1961-1972) and held professorships at Oslo (1974), Emory, Harvard, and Boston University (~1997-2008).

Friederike Assandri is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Nanjing University and Heidelberg University (Ph.D. 2002) under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer. She held visiting professorships at Humboldt, Leipzig, and Free University of Berlin.

Friedhelm Hardy was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Cologne, Münster, Heidelberg, and Oxford under Paul Hacker, Thomas Burrow, and Robert Charles Zaehner. He taught at King's College London and the University of Oxford.

Friedrich Adolf Krummacher was a religious studies scholar who studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from around 1785 to 1789. He held a post at the University of Duisburg from circa 1800 to 1807.

Friedrich Adolf Trendelenburg was a philosopher and linguist who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Berlin under Franz Bopp, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and August Boeckh. He held a long-term academic post at Frederick William University Berlin (~1833-1872).

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff studied Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies at the University of Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He served as professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1964-1982) and the University of Hamburg (1982-1993).

Friedrich August Rosen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and under Franz Bopp, Silvestre de Sacy, and Henry Colebrooke. He served as professor of Oriental Languages and Sanskrit at the University of London.

Friedrich August Wilhelm Krahmer was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Göttingen (~1829-1833) and served as Privatdozent of Oriental Languages at the University of Marburg from 1833 to 1840.
